citations.description: The _load_module helper implements cache-first logic but no test asserts the second-call identity invariant.

Exhaustive search for test_load_module_same, test_load_module_idempotent, test_load_module_cache, test_load_module_returns_same, assert first is second (in reconciler context), and all plausible variants returned no matches.

findings.criterion: a test asserts the helper returns the SAME object on a second call for the same name+path (one class object per name)
findings.detail: No test was found anywhere in the test suite that explicitly asserts `_load_module(name, path) is _load_module(name, path)` or equivalent. The `_load_module` helper in test_differ.py, test_differ_quarantine_suppression.py, and test_differ_conflict_resolution.py implements the cache-first logic (returning `cached` when name+path match), but no test exercises this path and asserts object identity on a second call. Exhaustive search by function name, ticket id, and key phrases returned no matches.

citations.description: The path guard is implemented (cached.__file__ == str(path)) but no test exercises the mismatch branch.

Exhaustive search for test_load_module_different_path, test_load_module_path_mismatch, test_load_module_path_guard, silently reuse, same-name/different-path, and all plausible variants returned no matches.

findings.criterion: a test asserts a same-name/different-path load does NOT silently reuse the wrong module
findings.detail: No test was found anywhere in the test suite that asserts the path-guard behavior: that when `sys.modules[name]` exists but its `__file__` does not match the requested path, `_load_module` loads a fresh module rather than returning the cached one. Exhaustive search by function name, ticket id, and key phrases returned no matches.
